response.sql:
WITH obs_with_phase AS (
  SELECT 
    t.bandusagepct,
    o.observstation,
    o.lunarstage
  FROM telescopes t
  INNER JOIN observatories o ON t.observstation = o.observstation
),
station_avgs AS (
  SELECT 
    lunarstage,
    observstation,
    AVG(bandusagepct) AS station_avg_bw
  FROM obs_with_phase
  WHERE bandusagepct IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY lunarstage, observstation
),
phase_bw AS (
  SELECT 
    lunarstage,
    AVG(station_avg_bw) AS avg_bw
  FROM station_avgs
  GROUP BY lunarstage
),
phase_count AS (
  SELECT 
    lunarstage,
    COUNT(DISTINCT observstation) AS num_stations
  FROM obs_with_phase
  GROUP BY lunarstage
),
total_stations AS (
  SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT observstation) AS total 
  FROM obs_with_phase
)
SELECT 
  pc.lunarstage AS phase,
  pb.avg_bw,
  pc.num_stations,
  pc.num_stations::REAL / ts.total::REAL AS fraction
FROM phase_count pc
LEFT JOIN phase_bw pb ON pc.lunarstage = pb.lunarstage
CROSS JOIN total_stations ts
ORDER BY pc.lunarstage

assumptions.assumption: The 'number of observatory stations in that phase' counts all distinct observstations with the given lunarstage, even if they have no non-NULL bandusagepct values (which would cause them to contribute NULL to the average bandwidth calculation).
If a lunar phase group has no stations with any non-NULL bandwidth values, the average bandwidth column is NULL in the output.
